new_statements.second_reader_evidence: The target lists only this one work and the reader opened it, so there were no silent or unopened listed works to spot-check. Instead I spot-checked the other files already saved in the byep1241 folder from our earlier reading: 8 'Byep' hits, all in the A80 classification/lexicostatistics appendix pp. 272ff and the Etter 1988 bibliography entry; no Byep phonology or stress), 3 hits: cluster membership, Table 1 code line 'A831 mkk byep1241 byep, north makaa', neighbouring-language remark; no Byep data) and the two SIL Cameroon the Internet Archive pages (no lexicon, no publications, no surveys). Nothing on Byep stress or tone was missed.

sources.citation: Heath, Daniel & Teresa Heath. 1982. A phonology of the Makaa language. Yaounde: SIL Cameroon (ms., WEB-BALL 8424).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Glottolog's 'Byep-Besep' includes Besep, which Heath treats as the Besip dialect of (South) Makaa; the Makaa phonology is the nearest first-hand description and may state Makaa (incl. Besip) stress/accent, usable only as a proxy with an identity caveat.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x langdoc query language=byep1241; WEB-BALL (reflex.cnrs.fr) LGNUM=mkk; HAL, theses.fr, archive.org, Zenodo, OpenAIRE, DOAJ, CrossRef keyword searches 'byep' / 'north makaa' / 'mekaa'.
sources.note: Glottolog and WEB-BALL each return exactly one reference (Etter 1988); the other indexes return no Byep-specific work.

sources.citation: Vermeir, Tessa. 2024. Analyses lexicales et phonologiques des langues A80 avec un focus sur le sso. These de doctorat (HAL tel-05296611).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Byep appears only in Table 1 (p.13, A831 mkk byep1241) and p.16 as a neighbouring language; not among the 10 LA80 languages; no Byep data, no stress statement for Byep (accent section 3.3.1 concerns Sso only).

sources.citation: Cheucle, Marion. 2014. Etude comparative des langues makaa-njem (bantu A80): phonologie, morphologie, lexique - vers une reconstruction du proto-A80. These de doctorat, Universite Lumiere Lyon 2 (theses.fr 2014LYO20071).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing on Byep. Sec. 4.6.2 (p.31): 'A ma connaissance, il n'existe aucune documentation disponible portant sur le byep, hormis un unique document (Etter 1988), demeurant inaccessible. Par consequent, il n'a pas ete envisage d'inclure cette langue dans la partie comparative.' Byep excluded from the comparative phonology.

sources.note: Byep mentioned only in the A80 classification / lexicostatistics appendix (p.272ff: Byep-Makaa-Kol-Konzime 'central cluster', 76% / 73.5% similarity figures; Besep speakers understand Byep, citing Heath 2003a:335). No Byep phonology, nothing on Byep stress.

sources.citation: Heath, Teresa. 2003. Makaa (A83). In Nurse & Philippson (eds.), The Bantu Languages, 335-348. London: Routledge.
